_comment: Example PhiGate price book, in Japanese yen.
Published list prices in USD are rarely what an enterprise actually pays:
Azure commitments, enterprise agreements and reseller contracts all differ.
Reporting savings at list price in a foreign currency is the fastest way to
have a finance team dismiss the number entirely.
Point PHIGATE_PRICE_BOOK at a file like this so /v1/phigate/stats and the
dashboard report in the currency and at the rates your CFO recognises.
local_per_million is the amortised cost of self-hosted inference. Leave it
at 0 to treat the marginal cost of an already-running Ollama as free, or
set it to (GPU hourly cost x hours) / (tokens served) for a fully-loaded
figure.
Domestic Japanese models are deliberately absent, for the same reason
Bedrock is absent from the built-in table: several of the models the
Digital Agency selected for Gennai are sold under enterprise or government
contracts with no published list rate, and inventing one would report a
number that is confidently wrong. Unmatched models are counted in
Totals.UnpricedRequests and surfaced by /v1/phigate/stats, so a deployment
can see that it owes this file an entry rather than quietly believing a
figure. Add your contracted rates here, prefix-matched on the model name:
{ "model": "plamo-", "input_per_million": 0, "output_per_million": 0 }
See docs/japan-models.md for which models these are and how to reach them.
_rates: Converted from each vendor's published USD list rate at JPY 150 = USD 1,
verified 2026-09-12. State your own rate and date when you edit this file:
a price book in yen with no recorded FX assumption cannot be reconciled
against a USD invoice, and nobody can tell whether a figure is stale.
Entries are matched LONGEST NAME FIRST, so a family name absorbs every
later generation that shares its prefix. This file previously listed
claude-opus-4 and none of the 4.x generations, which meant claude-opus-4-8
matched it and was reported at JPY 2250/11250 against a true 750/3750 —
three times the real cost, in a number a finance team was being asked to
trust. Enumerate every generation you actually call. A model with no entry
at all is the safe failure: it lands in Totals.UnpricedRequests and says so.
